currency.source: Placeholder exchange rate, update before quoting

pricing_status.source: Approximate vendor list prices entered manually (monthly, USD). Check the vendor page before quoting.

scales.small: Small (up to a few hundred users)
scales.large: Large (tens of thousands of users or more)

services.name: Vercel
services.why: Best developer experience for React, Next.js and Vue; preview deployments on every push.
services.hint: Import the Git repo, set the build command and environment variables, then assign your domain.

services.name: Netlify
services.why: Simple static and SPA hosting with forms, redirects and deploy previews.
services.hint: Connect the repo, set the publish directory and add a redirect rule for single-page routing.

services.name: Cloudflare Pages
services.why: Free, fast global network with generous limits; good value for static front ends.
services.hint: Connect the repo in the Cloudflare dashboard and set the build output directory.

services.name: AWS Amplify Hosting
services.why: Stays inside AWS if the rest of the system already runs there.
services.hint: Connect the repo in the Amplify console and configure build settings and environment variables.

services.name: Railway
services.why: Quick Git-based deploys with a Procfile, built-in variables and private networking.
services.hint: Create a service from the repo, add environment variables and set the start command (for example the Procfile).

services.name: Render
services.why: Predictable fixed prices, managed TLS and background workers.
services.hint: Create a Web Service from the repo, set build and start commands, and add environment variables.

services.name: Fly.io
services.why: Runs containers close to users in several regions.
services.hint: Write a Dockerfile, run the Fly launch command and set secrets with the Fly CLI.

services.name: DigitalOcean App Platform
services.why: Managed platform with straightforward pricing and a managed database option.
services.hint: Create an App from the repo, choose the component size and add environment variables.

services.name: AWS EC2 (self-managed)
services.why: Full control and the most flexibility, but you manage the server, updates and security.
services.hint: Launch an instance, install the runtime, run the app behind a process manager and a reverse proxy.

services.name: Neon (PostgreSQL)
services.why: Serverless PostgreSQL with branching; ideal while traffic is small or spiky.
services.hint: Create a project, copy the pooled connection string into DATABASE_URL and run your migrations.

services.name: Supabase (PostgreSQL)
services.why: PostgreSQL plus auth, storage and realtime in one platform.
services.hint: Create a project, copy the connection string into DATABASE_URL and run your migrations.

services.name: DigitalOcean Managed Database
services.why: Managed backups and failover with simple pricing.
services.hint: Create a managed cluster, restrict trusted sources and put the connection string in DATABASE_URL.

services.name: AWS RDS
services.why: Mature managed database with automated backups and Multi-AZ failover.
services.hint: Create the instance in a private subnet, open the port only to the backend security group.

services.name: MongoDB Atlas
services.why: The standard managed MongoDB service with backups and monitoring.
services.hint: Create a cluster, add the backend IP to the access list and put the URI in the environment.

services.name: Upstash Redis
services.why: Serverless Redis that bills by usage.
services.hint: Create a database and put its URL and token in the backend environment.

services.name: Redis Cloud
services.why: Managed Redis from Redis itself.
services.hint: Create a subscription and database, then set REDIS_URL.

services.name: AWS ElastiCache
services.why: Fits AWS-only architectures that need low latency inside a VPC.
services.hint: Create the cluster in a private subnet and allow only the backend security group.

services.name: AWS Application Load Balancer
services.why: Layer-7 routing and health checks for several backend instances.
services.hint: Create the load balancer, a target group and health-check path, then add TLS from ACM.

services.name: Cloudflare Load Balancing
services.why: DNS-level load balancing with failover across origins.
services.hint: Add your origins and a health monitor in the Cloudflare dashboard.

services.name: DigitalOcean Load Balancer
services.why: Simple managed load balancer if you already use DigitalOcean.
services.hint: Create the load balancer and attach your droplets or app.

services.name: AWS API Gateway
services.why: Managed gateway with throttling, authorizers and usage plans, billed per request.
services.hint: Create an HTTP API with an integration to the backend and enable throttling.

services.name: Kong Gateway (self-hosted)
services.why: Open-source gateway with plugins for rate limiting and auth; you run it yourself.
services.hint: Run Kong in a container next to the backend and define services and routes.

services.name: Alchemy
services.why: Reliable node access and APIs for EVM chains.
services.hint: Create an app for the target network and store the RPC URL and key as secrets.

services.name: Infura
services.why: Long-standing Ethereum node provider.
services.hint: Create a project, choose networks and store the endpoint and key as secrets.

services.name: QuickNode
services.why: Many supported chains and add-ons.
services.hint: Create an endpoint for the target chain and store the URL as a secret.

services.name: Cloudflare R2
services.why: S3-compatible storage with no egress fees.
services.hint: Create a bucket and an API token, then use the S3-compatible endpoint.

services.name: AWS S3
services.why: The default choice for object storage on AWS.
services.hint: Create a private bucket, block public access and use an IAM role for the backend.

services.name: Backblaze B2
services.why: Low storage cost with an S3-compatible API.
services.hint: Create a bucket and an application key for the backend.

services.name: Cloudflare CDN
services.why: CDN, DNS, TLS and basic DDoS protection in one place.
services.hint: Point your nameservers to Cloudflare and enable proxying for the site.

services.name: AWS CloudFront
services.why: CDN that integrates with S3 and the rest of AWS.
services.hint: Create a distribution with your origin and attach a TLS certificate.

services.name: Bunny CDN
services.why: Low-cost CDN with simple pricing.
services.hint: Create a pull zone pointing at your origin.

services.name: Qdrant Cloud
services.why: Managed Qdrant, the vector database you already use for RAG.
services.hint: Create a cluster and put its URL and API key in QDRANT_URL and QDRANT_API_KEY.

services.name: Pinecone
services.why: Fully managed vector database.
services.hint: Create an index with the right dimension and store the API key.

services.name: Sentry
services.why: Error tracking and performance monitoring for both front end and back end.
services.hint: Add the SDK to the app and set the DSN as an environment variable.

services.name: Grafana Cloud
services.why: Metrics, logs and dashboards in one hosted stack.
services.hint: Install the agent and send metrics and logs to your stack.

services.name: UptimeRobot
services.why: Simple uptime checks and alerts.
services.hint: Add an HTTP check for the health endpoint and set alert contacts.

services.name: GitHub Actions
services.why: Built in to GitHub; easy pipelines for tests and deploys.
services.hint: Add a workflow that runs tests and deploys on merge to the main branch.

services.name: GitLab CI/CD
services.why: Pipelines inside GitLab with good environment tracking.
services.hint: Add a pipeline file that runs tests and deploys from the main branch.

services.name: Resend
services.why: Developer-friendly transactional email API.
services.hint: Verify your sending domain and store the API key as a secret.

services.name: Amazon SES
services.why: Very low cost per email; needs more set-up.
services.hint: Verify the domain, request production access and use SMTP or the API.

services.name: Brevo
services.why: Transactional and marketing email with a free tier.
services.hint: Verify the sender domain and store the SMTP or API key as a secret.
